records.name: Davao Region
records.summary: This division was covered by the dedicated country dossier, which identified no deviation from the national position material enough to score separately (±0.02); it is therefore assessed at the national score. The attached sources are national-level rather than regional: a country-organisation overview of the national legal picture, a June 2025 report on the killing of an 18-year-old trans woman in a different province (Cagayan), and a national news item on a case in another region (Batangas) that could not be retrieved at fetch time.

records.name: Caraga
records.summary:
Caraga has no documented region-specific laws affecting transgender people; the national framework is what applies here: same-sex conduct is legal, there is no legal gender-recognition pathway, national SOGIE equality legislation has been filed since 1999 without enactment, and anti-discrimination ordinances exist only at some city and provincial levels. The Safe Spaces Act criminalises homophobic and transphobic slurs, school anti-bullying rules and gender-responsive education policy cover SOGI grounds, and executive orders created a national diversity-and-inclusion programme that, per audited reporting, remained unimplemented as of 2025.

Acceptance runs partial: a 2018 national survey recorded about one-fifth support for same-sex civil unions and majority opposition to trans women's use of women's toilets. A June 2025 report on the killing of an eighteen-year-old trans student, which a national alliance presented as part of a pattern of violence against trans Filipinas, originates in a different region — it is Caraga only as part of the archipelago-wide climate, and is recorded as exactly that.
